message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"1.13","text":"While I was saying these things and what followed from them, a great uproar arose among the crowds. Some, out of pity for Barnabas, took my side, but others, being foolish, fiercely gnashed their teeth at me. When evening had finally overtaken us, I took Barnabas by the hand and forcibly led him, though he was unwilling, to my house. There I also made him stay, so that no one might lay hands on him. After remaining for a few days and briefly instructing me in the word of truth (a little, given the few days), he said that he was hurrying to Judaea for the sake of the festival observed according to his religion, and he wanted from then on to be with his own fellow countrymen.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"συνήραντό μοι","chosen":"took my side","rationale":"The expression indicates joining Clement in support of Barnabas; alternatives include “joined me” and the more literal “helped lift with me.”"},{"source_quote":"δεινῶς κατ’ ἐμοῦ ἔβρυχον τοὺς ὀδόντας","chosen":"fiercely gnashed their teeth at me","rationale":"Preserves both the hostile force of δεινῶς and the physical image of grinding or gnashing the teeth."},{"source_quote":"βραχέα κατηχήσας με","chosen":"briefly instructing me","rationale":"κατηχέω denotes oral instruction here; the context does not require the later technical sense of formal catechesis."},{"source_quote":"τῆς κατὰ τὴν θρησκείαν ἑορτῆς","chosen":"the festival observed according to his religion","rationale":"This retains the passage’s characterization of the festival through θρησκεία without identifying or harmonizing it with a particular named observance."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ ὁμοεθνέσιν","chosen":"his own fellow countrymen","rationale":"ὁμοεθνής denotes people belonging to the same nation or ethnic community."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"1.14","text":"But it was plain to me that he had become reluctant. For I said, “You need only set out for me the words you heard from the man who appeared, and I, after adorning them with my own discourse, will proclaim the will of God. Then, within a few days, I will sail with you, for I greatly long to reach the regions of Judaea. Perhaps I will even live with you for the entire course of my life.” But when he heard this, he answered, “If you wish to investigate our affairs and learn what is beneficial, sail with me at once. At any rate, today I will tell you the directions to my lodging and to those whom you wish to find, so that whenever you want, you may come and join us. For tomorrow I will depart for my own place.” And so, seeing that he was unyielding, I went with him as far as the harbor. After learning from him the directions to the residences that he had mentioned, I said to him, “If it were not that tomorrow I am to collect something owed to me, I would sail with you at once. Nevertheless, I will catch up with you very soon.” After saying this and entrusting him to the ship’s officers, I went back sorrowfully, thinking of my good and intimate friend.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"φανερὸς δ’ ἦν μοι ἀποναρκήσας","chosen":"But it was plain to me that he had become reluctant","rationale":"ἀποναρκάω can suggest becoming numb, indifferent, weary, or disinclined. “Reluctant” fits Barnabas’s refusal to remain and instruct Clement on Clement’s terms."},{"source_quote":"κἀγὼ τῷ ἐμῷ κοσμήσας λόγῳ","chosen":"and I, after adorning them with my own discourse","rationale":"κοσμέω retains the potentially self-confident claim that Clement would embellish or ornament the reported words with his own presentation."},{"source_quote":"ἐξ αὐτῆς μοι σύμπλευσον","chosen":"sail with me at once","rationale":"In this context ἐξ αὐτῆς functions idiomatically as “immediately” or “at once.”"},{"source_quote":"ἱστορῆσαι τὰ ἡμέτερα","chosen":"investigate our affairs","rationale":"ἱστορέω means to inquire into or learn by investigation, rather than merely to write a history."},{"source_quote":"καὶ δὴ ἀδυσώπητον ἰδὼν","chosen":"And so, seeing that he was unyielding","rationale":"ἀδυσώπητος describes someone who cannot be moved by entreaty; “inexorable” is a possible but less accessible alternative."},{"source_quote":"Εἰ μὴ ὅτι αὔριόν τι ἀπαιτῶ ὀφειλόμενόν μοι","chosen":"If it were not that tomorrow I am to collect something owed to me","rationale":"ἀπαιτέω here means to demand or collect what is due, while τι leaves the precise object unspecified."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς τοῦ πλοίου ἡγουμένοις","chosen":"the ship’s officers","rationale":"The phrase denotes those directing or commanding the vessel; alternatives include “leaders” and “captains.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἐπεί γε τὰ σημεῖα τῆς οἰκήσεώς μου καὶ ὧν θέλεις ἐγώ σοι σήμερον ἐρῶ","issue":"The attachment and referent of ὧν θέλεις are ambiguous. The rendering takes it as referring to people whose identifying directions Clement wants, while alternatives include “the things you want” or treating the phrase as further information about Barnabas’s lodging. ἐπεί γε may be causal (“since indeed”) or transitional (“at any rate”); the latter better preserves the flow without supplying an omitted condition.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"1.15","text":"After spending some days there and being unable to recover the debt in full, I disregarded what remained for the sake of speed, since it was an impediment, and I myself sailed to Judaea. After fifteen days I arrived at Caesarea of Straton. When I had set foot on land and was looking for lodging, I learned that a certain man called Peter—the most highly approved disciple of the man who had appeared in Judaea and had performed signs and wonders—was to hold a verbal debate the next day with Simon, the Samaritan from Gittha. When I heard this, I asked that Peter’s lodging be pointed out to me. I nevertheless learned where it was and came to the gateway. When those in the house saw me, they questioned me about who I was and where I had come from. And behold, Barnabas came out and, as soon as he saw me, embraced me, rejoicing greatly and weeping. Taking me by the hand, he led me inside to where Peter was and said to me, “This is Peter, whom I declared to you to be greatest in the wisdom of God. I spoke to him about you continually, as you will learn for yourself, for I truthfully related all the good things about you and at the same time disclosed your resolve, with the result that he himself is eager to see you as well. Therefore, through my own hands I present you to him as a great gift.” After saying this, he presented me and said, “This is Clement, Peter.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τάχους ἕνεκα ἀμελήσας τοῦ περιλειφθέντος ὡς ἐμποδίου ὄντος","chosen":"I disregarded what remained for the sake of speed, since it was an impediment","rationale":"The remainder is the unpaid portion of the debt; the translation preserves Clement’s characterization of waiting for it as an obstacle."},{"source_quote":"Καισάρειαν κατήντησα τὴν Στράτωνος","chosen":"I arrived at Caesarea of Straton","rationale":"The genitive distinguishes the city conventionally known as Caesarea Maritima or Straton’s Caesarea without replacing the source’s wording."},{"source_quote":"ξενίαν θηρωμένου","chosen":"was looking for lodging","rationale":"θηράω literally evokes hunting or seeking; here its object ξενία indicates a search for lodging or hospitality."},{"source_quote":"ὁ δοκιμώτατος ὑπάρχων μαθητής","chosen":"the most highly approved disciple","rationale":"δοκιμώτατος can mean most tested, approved, esteemed, or distinguished; “highly approved” retains its evaluative force."},{"source_quote":"ζήτησιν ποιεῖται λόγων","chosen":"was to hold a verbal debate","rationale":"The expression denotes an examination or dispute conducted through words; alternatives include “discussion” and “debate of arguments.”"},{"source_quote":"καὶ ὁμῶς ἔμαθον","chosen":"I nevertheless learned where it was","rationale":"ὁμῶς can convey “all the same” or “equally”; in context it functions naturally as “nevertheless.” The supplied spelling is retained as an edition feature rather than treated as an OCR error."},{"source_quote":"ἀντέβαλλον τίς τε ὢν καὶ πόθεν ἥκω","chosen":"they questioned me about who I was and where I had come from","rationale":"ἀντιβάλλω has the contextual sense of putting questions or statements to someone, not merely its literal sense of throwing one thing against another."},{"source_quote":"ὡς εἴσει ἐκ ταὐτομάτου","chosen":"as you will learn for yourself","rationale":"The phrase suggests knowledge arising directly or spontaneously from what occurs; alternatives include “from the event itself” and “directly.”"},{"source_quote":"διὰ τῶν ἐμῶν προσφέρω χειρῶν","chosen":"through my own hands I present you","rationale":"The wording preserves Barnabas’s image of personally presenting Clement as a gift."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τὸ χρέος οὐχ. ὅλον λαβεῖν δυνηθείς","issue":"The printed period after οὐχ interrupts the otherwise straightforward phrase “unable to receive the debt in full.” It appears to be anomalous editorial punctuation rather than missing content.","proposed_reading":"τὸ χρέος οὐχ ὅλον λαβεῖν δυνηθείς","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"τοῦ σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα· πεποιηκότος","issue":"The printed middle dot separates the object σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα from πεποιηκότος, although the article τοῦ and participle naturally form the phrase “the one who had performed signs and wonders.” The translation treats the punctuation as non-syntactic; the supplied wording remains intelligible.","proposed_reading":"τοῦ σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα πεποιηκότος","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἅμα καὶ τὴν προαίρεσιν ἐξέφανα, ὡς αὐτὸν γλίχεσθαι καὶ ἰδεῖν σε","issue":"The relation introduced by ὡς is ambiguous. The translation reads it as a result of Barnabas’s disclosure of Clement’s resolve: Peter consequently became eager to see Clement. It could instead introduce a report or explanation, “the intention—that he was eager to see you,” though that gives προαίρεσιν a less clear referent.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"1.16","text":"Good Peter sprang forward as soon as he heard my name and kissed me warmly. After making me sit down, he immediately said, “You did well when, in honor of the God who truly is, you nobly hosted Barnabas, the herald of truth, without being ashamed or fearing the anger of the uneducated crowds. You will be blessed. For just as you hosted the ambassador of truth with every honor, so truth itself will make you, though a stranger to its own city, a citizen. Then you will rejoice greatly because you have now lent a brief favor (by which I mean a resolve for good words). You will be an heir of eternal and inalienable good things. And do not weary yourself describing your character to me, for Barnabas, who does not lie, has related everything about you to us, making favorable mention of you almost every day. To tell you briefly, as a genuine friend, what lies before us: if nothing hinders you, travel with us and share in the discourses of truth that I am about to deliver city by city, all the way to Rome itself. And you too, if there is anything you wish, speak.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"κατεφίλησεν","chosen":"kissed me warmly","rationale":"The compound verb can indicate affectionate or repeated kissing; “warmly” conveys its intensity without specifying an unsupported number of kisses."},{"source_quote":"εἰς τιμὴν τοῦ ὄντως θεοῦ","chosen":"in honor of the God who truly is","rationale":"ὁ ὄντως θεός can mean “the true God,” but the chosen wording more directly preserves the existential force of ὄντως."},{"source_quote":"τὸν τῆς ἀληθείας πρεσβευτὴν","chosen":"the ambassador of truth","rationale":"πρεσβευτής denotes an authorized envoy or ambassador; “messenger” is possible but less specific."},{"source_quote":"ξένον ὄντα τῆς ἰδίας πόλεως καταστήσει πολίτην","chosen":"will make you, though a stranger to its own city, a citizen","rationale":"The rendering preserves the contrast between ξένος and πολίτης. The genitive may attach more closely to either “stranger” or “citizen,” but the civic metaphor remains the same."},{"source_quote":"βραχεῖαν νῦν ἐδάνεισας χάριν","chosen":"you have now lent a brief favor","rationale":"ἐδάνεισας preserves the metaphor of lending, while βραχεῖαν may describe the favor as brief or small; “brief” suits the contrast with eternal benefits."},{"source_quote":"ἀιδίων καὶ ἀναφαιρέτων ἀγαθῶν","chosen":"eternal and inalienable good things","rationale":"ἀναφαίρετος describes what cannot be taken away; alternatives include “irrevocable” and “unremovable.”"},{"source_quote":"μὴ κάμνε ἀντιβάλλειν μοι τὸ σὸν ἦθος","chosen":"do not weary yourself describing your character to me","rationale":"κάμνω with the infinitive means to grow weary in doing something, and ἀντιβάλλω here means to set forth or relate."},{"source_quote":"σχεδὸν καθ᾿ ἡμέραν τὴν ἀγαθήν σου ποιούμενος μνήμην","chosen":"making favorable mention of you almost every day","rationale":"ποιεῖσθαι μνήμην means to make mention or remembrance; ἀγαθήν marks that mention as favorable."},{"source_quote":"ὧν κατὰ πόλιν ποιεῖσθαι μέλλω μέχρι Ῥώμης αὐτῆς","chosen":"that I am about to deliver city by city, all the way to Rome itself","rationale":"ποιεῖσθαι λόγους denotes giving or delivering discourses, while κατὰ πόλιν indicates successive activity in each city."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"προαίρεσιν λόγων καλῶν λέγων","issue":"The parenthetical expression is semantically compressed. The rendering takes λόγων καλῶν as an objective genitive, “a resolve for good words or discourses,” and λέγων as clarifying what Peter means by the “favor.” Alternatives include “a preference for good discourses” and “a good disposition expressed in words.”","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ξένον ὄντα τῆς ἰδίας πόλεως καταστήσει πολίτην","issue":"The genitive τῆς ἰδίας πόλεως can be heard with ξένον (“a stranger to its own city”) or with πολίτην (“a citizen of its own city”). The main rendering allows the city to remain associated with both sides of the stranger/citizen contrast.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
